title: Living Under a Lethal Sky: Myanmar’s Rakhine on Edge as Military Airstrikes on Civilians Grow
gist: An eyewitness account from Yoe Ngu village in Ponnagyun township, Rakhine State, Myanmar, where an airstrike on February 24, 2026 destroyed a market serving three villages and left burnt body parts among the ruins. Hours later the village was deserted except for a few men searching the ashes for remains.

insights.claim: An airstrike on Yoe Ngu village in Ponnagyun township, Rakhine State, Myanmar, on February 24, 2026 destroyed a thriving market that served three villages, leaving mutilated and burnt body parts amid bombed houses.
insights.so_what: Strikes on civilian markets in Rakhine signal escalating air war in Myanmar's conflict, with implications for humanitarian access and regional displacement.
insights.quote: Smoke billowed from what was once a thriving market selling a wide range of commodities and catering to the needs of three villages in the area.
insights.speaker: Rajeev Bhattacharyya

insights.claim: By 7:30 p.m. on the day of the strike, Yoe Ngu village was deserted except for six men using torches, sticks and shovels to search through ash and charred heaps.
insights.so_what: Rapid abandonment of villages after strikes indicates mass internal displacement in Rakhine State.
insights.locator: When I arrived at the bombed site
insights.speaker: Rajeev Bhattacharyya

insights.claim: A day after the airstrike, residents of Yoe Ngu village were searching for the bodies of their kin, indicating heavy civilian casualties.
insights.so_what: Documented civilian deaths from airstrikes feed international accountability pressure on Myanmar's conflict actors.
insights.speaker: Rajeev Bhattacharyya
